physiology:
The traditions seat this code in the thyroid, the small butterfly of tissue at the front of the throat, and in the parathyroids tucked behind it. The thyroid sets the metabolic pace of the whole body. It decides how fast the cells burn, how warm the blood runs, how quickly hunger comes back after eating. It is the gland that keeps adjusting the dial on the engine of you.

The shadow has its bodily floor here. The restless wanting that drives the card lives at the throat. A faint constriction at the front of the neck, a swallowing that is not quite empty and not quite full, a heat under the jaw when something half delivers and the urge to chase the next thing fires up again. The body keeps speeding the metabolism to chase a fullness the outside world cannot supply. Days run thin, sleep stays light, the engine runs hot for no reward.

The climb is also bodily. The throat softens before any decision is made. The pulse there steadies. The pace of the body finds its own rhythm rather than the rhythm the wanting was driving it to. Warmth spreads from the front of the neck down into the chest, and the chase loosens its grip. The metabolism stops outrunning life. The gland that was set to chase, gets to set itself to feel.
amino_acid:
Deeper than the gland, this code answers to a single amino acid, tryptophan. Tryptophan belongs to the small group the body cannot make for itself. It must be taken in, carried across the line of the mouth from somewhere outside, broken down, and only then put to use. Once inside, it is the precursor the body uses to build serotonin, the chemistry of satiation, the molecule that says, enough, this is enough.

There is a teaching in that, and it is the whole card written in chemistry. The code whose shadow is hunger is built on the very letter the body cannot make for itself. The fullness it craves is not something it can manufacture on its own. It has to be received. And when received, it becomes the signal for stopping. The hunger and its end share one amino acid. The card runs all the way down to this: a wanting that becomes, at the right moment, the chemistry of having had enough.
